ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, two sides BA and BC are drawn from point B to form angle ABC, and ray BP is located inside this angle. At B there are two identical pink arcs, indicating that ∠ABP and ∠PBC are equal, so BP is the angle bisector of ∠ABC. From point P to side BA there is line segment PA, and at A there is a right-angle mark, showing that PA⊥BA; from point P to side BC there is line segment PC, and at C there is a right-angle mark, showing that PC⊥BC. Beside PA in the figure is marked length 8. Reasoning: Point P is on angle bisector BP, and a point on an angle bisector has equal perpendicular distances to the two sides of the angle. PA and PC are exactly the perpendicular distances from point P to the two sides BA and BC, so PC=PA=8.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that ray BP lies inside angle ABC and the pink angle marks at B show ∠ABP = ∠PBC, so BP is the angle bisector. Also read the right-angle marks: AP is perpendicular to BA and CP is perpendicular to BC, making AP and CP the perpendicular distances from point P to the two sides of the angle. The image labels AP = 8. From the text, the task is to find CP. Use the angle-bisector distance property: any point on an angle bisector is equidistant from the two sides of the angle. Therefore CP = AP = 8.
